testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What is the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi of air per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, what does it do?

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows the vehicle.

questions.question: How is the parking brake applied in newer vehicles?

options.text: Move a lever to the right

questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob to apply the brakes and push it to release them.

questions.question: When should you avoid using the parking brake?

options.text: When the brakes are very hot
When the brakes are very cold
When there is snow on the ground

questions.correctAnswerText: When the brakes are very hot
questions.explanation: Do not use the parking brake when the brakes are hot from going down a steep grade. Let the brakes cool first to avoid damage.

questions.question: What happens if you do not drain air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure
Too much air collects in the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks regularly to remove water and compressor oil. In cold weather, frozen water can cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: What happens when ABS is only on one axle?

options.text: You still have more control when braking
It slows the vehicle but cannot stop it

questions.correctAnswerText: You still have more control when braking
questions.explanation: Even with ABS on only one axle, you have better braking control than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do when air pressure reaches 125 psi?

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air
Begin pumping air into the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air
questions.explanation: At 125 psi, the air compressor governor stops the compressor from pumping. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: Brake linings should be:
questions.explanation: Brake linings must be clean and dry. They should not have oil or grease on them. They should not be too thin or loose.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air:

options.text: There is something wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is something wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the brake system. Have a mechanic check it before driving.

questions.question: When operating a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the driver should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving to ensure that the fuel reaches the engine.
Let the air compressor build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in the primary and secondary systems before driving.
Begin driving just after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in the primary and secondary systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving, wait for the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. Watch the air pressure gauges to check the pressure.

questions.question: You should test the low pressure warning signal by:

options.text: Turning on the engine and applying the trailer hand brake.
Rapidly pressing and releasing the brake pedal.
Removing wheel chocks and disengaging the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rapidly pressing and releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: After the system is charged, test the warning light by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the system. The warning light should come on when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake is caused when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction is created when the brake shoes and linings push against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should ensure that the ____ come on automatically when air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Check that spring brakes come on automatically when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Test this by chocking the wheels and releasing air by stepping on and off the brake pedal. The parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should engage.

questions.question: A ____ allows a driver to gradually apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver slowly apply spring brakes. It is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it is attached to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before each trip, check the slack adjusters. Pull them gently to make sure they move only about one inch from the push rod. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment by a mechanic.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Test the brakes while driving, but continue driving if nothing seems wrong.
Drive with the hazard lights activated.

questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and park the vehicle as soon as safely possible. You must stop while you still have braking power left.

questions.question: If an air compressor is belt-driven, the belt should be routinely checked to ensure that it is:
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each trip. Make sure it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: What shows you the air pressure in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

questions.question: When should a low air pressure warning signal turn on?

options.text: When tank pressure falls below 120 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 60 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 10 psi.
When tank pressure falls below 5 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure falls below 60 psi.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning must turn on when air pressure drops below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, a buzzer, or a wig wag.

questions.question: What stops your wheels from locking up during braking?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you apply the brakes.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in an air brake system is releasing air, what does this mean?

options.text: You should not be concerned as this is a normal process.
There is something wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is something wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if pressure gets too high. If it releases air, something is wrong. Have a mechanic fix it.

questions.question: If air pressure drops to between ____, the low pressure warning light should already be on.
questions.explanation: The low pressure warning light should turn on before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. The warning can be a light, a buzzer, or a wig wag.
